title: NZ vs IND: Jasprit Bumrah Surpasses Javagal Srinath To Enter Top 10 List Of Indian Wicket Taker In Tests
text:

 Bumrah surpassed Javagal Srinath with 3 wickets on Day 1 of the first Test between India and New Zealand to enter the the Top 10 list of the Indian wicket takers in Test cricket.
 by Chetan Phore | Nov 19, 2026 | 2 mins read Bumrah surpasses Srinath in the Top 10 list · Credits; Via BCCI Cricket Indian speedstar Jasprit Bumrah has immediately made an impact on his comeback game for the Indian senior team after dealing with his prolonged injury and subsequent rehabilitations in the Day 1 of the first Test match between India and New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington. With his three wickets in the first day of the game, Bumrah surpassed former Indian bowler Javagal Srinath to enter the Top 10 list of Indian wicket takers in Test cricket with 237 wickets.
 Bumrah took 53 red ball games to reach this milestone which is 14 less than Srinath as he reached the milestone in 67 Tests. Srinath had 234 wickets to his name so Bumrah surpassed him after clinching three wickets in the first day of the ongoing Test. Bumrah started to show his class from the first over itself as he surprised the skipper Tom Latham by dismissing him for a duck as he tried to leave a delivery of his which was travelling outside the off stump and ended up being clean bowled.
 🚨 JASPRIT BUMRAH INTO TOP 10 WICKET TAKERS LIST OF INDIAN TEST HISTORY 🐐
- Bumrah overtook Srinath and he is currently 10th in the list with 237 wickets.
The Greatest Indian bowler ever. https://t.co/WeXNhdcAwR
— CricGlobal (@CricGlobal000) November 19, 2026 
 Bumrah got his second wicket by dismissing Daryl Mitchell for just 1 run from 8 balls in the 21st over. Mitchell threw his wicket by handing a catch to Yashasvi Jaiswal at forward short leg. His third wicket came in the form of Tom Blundell as he removed him in the 29th over. Blundell gave away a catch at slip to skipper Shubman Gill. Gill spotted the ball late but still somehow managed to grab it by jumping to his right and using his leg as a cover.
 India’s All-Time Top 10 Test Wicket Takers
 Anil Kumble: 619 wickets
 Ravichandran Ashwin: 537 wickets
 Kapil Dev: 434 wickets
 Harbhajan Singh: 417 wickets
 Ravindra Jadeja: 356 wickets
 Ishant Sharma: 311 wickets
 Zaheer Khan: 311 wickets
 Bishan Singh Bedi: 266 wickets
 Bhagwath Chandrasekhar: 242 wickets
 Jasprit Bumrah: 237 wickets
 Why His Numbers Stand Out in Indian Test History?
 Bumrah holds an unbelievable average of 19.74 in Test cricket and is the only bowler in the Top 10 list to achieve this as R. Ashwin sits behind him with an average of 24.00.
 Bumrah has a higher strike rate than any other Indian fast bowler in the history as he has already left behind the legends like Mohammed Shami (50.28) and Zaheer Khan (60.40).
 Unlike other bowlers, Bumrah has maintained equal dominance on both home and away conditions as he holds good records in SENA countries as well.
 Currently, sitting at number 10, Bumrah is five wickets behind ninth placed B.S. Chandrasekhar (242) and 29 wickets behind eighth placed Bishan Singh Bedi (266). He is fourth among Indian fast bowlers with Kapil Dev, Ishant Sharma and Zaheer Khan ahead of him.
 NZ vs IND Day 1 Summary
 NZ (1st innings): 243/5 (82 overs)
 Glenn Phillips*: 94 (182)
 Henry Nicholls*: 113 (221)
 Jasprit Bumrah: 3/52 (17 overs)
